author: clean-loop8 SME critic (independent Claude critic subagent, 2026-11-19)

findings.claim: The loop-8 residual wording is accurate for every case it names, but two of its clauses are scoped more narrowly than the test behaves, so it still does not state the residual in full. The same two clauses appear in the solved-run record's not-covered list (authoring/evidence/html-css-js/html-and-css/coding-lab-solved-run.json line 49). (a) 'A finite animation is finished to its end whatever its play state or delay' is true only for the gear checklist and the two tags: the test calls finish() only on the elements in its quiet list (.site-aside, .pack-tag-day, .pack-tag-overnight). A finite animation on an element around the checklist is not finished and is read at one instant, but the text names elements around the checklist only under 'an endless one'. On a fresh git archive of 7e1a2af6 with the private completed work plus one added rule each, full suite, these passed all 12 tests in 3 of 3 runs: a forwards-filled reduced individual scale on .page with a delay of a few seconds, longer than the test takes; the same with the transform function on .page and .site-main; and a very long (thousands of seconds) linear forwards-filled scale-down on .page. Opened unmodified in the pinned Chromium at 1280x1000, each draws both tags at 200px when first sampled and at another width at later samples (the delayed ones after the delay, the very long one at 30s and 60s). Controls: the same delayed rule on .site-aside failed task 11 in 3 of 3 runs with the checklist message, and on the tags in 3 of 3 with the unscaled message, which confirms the finish-then-check path covers only those three elements. (b) 'so a paused, long-delayed or very long one that ends at the expected values passes' describes the condition by the animation's end keyframe. What is measured after finish() is the held end: the last keyframe when the fill mode is forwards or both, otherwise no effect at all, so the unanimated values are measured (Web Animations fill behaviour). A paused finite animation on both tags with fill mode backwards, whose keyframes both hold a reduced scale, passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs while the page draws both tags at another width at every sample (0.3s, 1.5s, 4s); its end keyframe is not an expected value. Control: the same rule with fill mode both failed task 11 in 3 of 3. Why low and not medium like cl7-sme-001: the passage opens with the general 'It does not detect every animation that changes the drawn size', its preceding sentence already scopes finishing to 'finite animations on them', the clause 'An animation still running is read at one moment' is literally true of a delayed ancestor animation (its play state is running), elements around the checklist are named as a category, and README task 11 Outcome (line 141) forbids every one of these variants. What is left is a missing scope qualifier and a narrow example, not a category of passing wrong pages that no text names. This is a description gap only and falls inside the owner's option A residual; no detection change is asked for.

evidence.section: 4.6 Fill behavior and 4.8.3.1 Calculating the active time (after the active interval, the active time is unresolved unless the fill mode is forwards or both, so an effect without a forwards fill stops applying)
4.4.13 Finishing an animation (sets the current time to the associated effect end whatever the play state, cancelling a pending pause)

findings.recommendation: Wording only, in lab.json notes and in the next solved-run record's not-covered list, with no test change. For example: 'Only animations on the checklist and the two tags are finished. A finite one is finished whatever its play state or delay and then measured at its held end (its last keyframe with a forwards fill, otherwise the unanimated values), so a paused, long-delayed or very long one passes when that held end is right. Every other animation is read at one moment, so an endless one on the checklist or the tags can pass in some or all runs when it changes a width or padding, rests at none for part of each cycle or pulses the checklist zoom, and any animation, finite or endless, on an element around the checklist can pass. Animated custom properties are not inspected.' Optionally add a delayed finite scale on .page and a paused non-forwards-filled scale on the tags to the record's list of known undetected variants.

items.note: The record's not-covered list (line 49) and lab.json notes (line 87) no longer restrict the residual to width or padding. Both now name the four cases cl7-sme-001 reported, and each reproduces on a fresh archive of 7e1a2af6 with the private completed work plus one rule, full suite, with the page drawn wrong in the same Chromium without test handling: (1) a paused finite animation holding a reduced scale on both tags and ending at identity passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs, drawn wrong at 3 of 3 samples; (2) an endless transform pulse on the tags resting at none for most of each cycle passed 3 of 3, drawn wrong at 3 of 6 samples; (3) an endless zoom pulse on .site-aside resting at 1 passed 3 of 3, drawn wrong at 3 of 6; (4) an endless scale pulse from 1 on .page passed 3 of 3, drawn wrong at 6 of 6. An endless width animation on the day tag passed 5 of 5 and an endless padding animation on the overnight tag 5 of 5, matching 'can pass in some or all runs when it changes a width or padding'. 'Animated custom properties are not inspected' is true: the test never inspects which properties an animation touches. The record's other claims match current bytes: every artifactHashes value equals the 7e1a2af6 bytes, commit and procedure name 7e1a2af6, and the starter and solved runs reproduce (see report reply). Two remaining scope gaps in the new wording (finite animations around the checklist; the held end without a forwards fill) are reported as cl8-sme-001, low.

Test bytes are unchanged since 80eff5af (same sha256). Loop-6 regression part stays closed: unscaledNow applies the strict none/'1' comparison while any animation on the element is unfinished. On a fresh archive of 7e1a2af6 with the private completed work plus one rule each, full suite, each failed task 11 and only task 11 in 5 of 5 runs: an endless alternating scale pulse from 1 on both tags; an endless rotate 1turn spin; an endless transform rotate(360deg) spin; an endless scale pulse from 1 on .site-aside, with the checklist message. A paused endless reduced scale on the tags failed 3 of 3. Older part (endless width or padding read at one instant): the owner chose option A, so it is a documented residual, and lab.json line 87 and record line 49 now state it honestly as 'can pass in some or all runs when it changes a width or padding'. Confirmed: an endless width animation on the day tag passed all 12 in 5 of 5 runs while drawn wrong at every sample, and an endless padding animation on the overnight tag passed 5 of 5.

All three original variants fail task 11, and only task 11, in 3 of 3 runs each on a fresh archive of 7e1a2af6 with the private completed work plus one rule: (a) a short forwards-filled animation holding another width on .pack-tag-day fails on the layout-width assertion; (b) an endless scale animation on both tags that never reaches identity fails on the unscaled assertion; (c) a short forwards-filled animation holding another padding on .pack-tag-overnight fails on the padding assertion. Animations are not forced off: finite ones on the checklist and tags are finished and the held end is measured.
